With $\beta>0$ and real $\epsilon$ the Fermi function can be written as
\begin{align}
\frac{1}{e^{\beta\epsilon}+1} &= \frac{1}{2} \nonumber\\
&\quad - \frac{1}{2}\tanh\left(\frac{\beta\epsilon}{2}\right) = \frac{e^{-\beta\epsilon}}{1+e^{-\beta\epsilon}} .
\label{eq:nf}
\end{align}
